The Executive Director of Accreditation and Evaluation provides strategic leadership, oversight, and operational management for the School of Nursing's accreditation, educational effectiveness, assessment, program evaluation, regulatory compliance, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) enterprise. Reporting to the Associate Dean for Academic and Faculty Affairs, the position serves as the School's senior authority on accreditation, educational quality, and evidence-based program evaluation, ensuring compliance with national, state, university, and professional accreditation requirements while advancing a culture of continuous improvement and academic excellence.
Accreditation Leadership & Compliance

The Executive Director leads the development and implementation of an integrated framework for accreditation readiness, educational assessment, outcomes evaluation, and quality improvement across all academic programs. Utilizing advanced program evaluation methodologies and qualitative and quantitative approaches to assessing educational effectiveness, the position oversees the systems, processes, and performance measures used to evaluate program quality, student success, faculty effectiveness, and institutional outcomes.
Provides senior leadership and organizational oversight for accreditation and regulatory compliance activities across all academic programs within the School of Nursing.

The Executive Director develops and maintains an integrated framework for accreditation readiness, assessment, outcomes evaluation, and continuous quality improvement across all educational programs. The position collaborates closely with school leadership, program directors, faculty, staff, and institutional partners to ensure ongoing compliance, data-driven decision-making, and educational excellence.
Serves as the School's principal liaison with accrediting and regulatory agencies and provides strategic guidance to program leadership to support accreditation success.

As the School's senior non-executive leader responsible for accreditation and educational effectiveness, the Executive Director plays a critical role in safeguarding accreditation status, advancing educational quality, supporting student success, informing strategic planning, and ensuring the successful implementation, continuation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of existing and future nursing and health professions programs. Through the leadership of subordinate managers and professional staff, the position directly influences institutional reputation, program viability, operational excellence, and the School's long-term strategic growth.
